component.name: Spinus DAW
component.summary: Make music with patterns, a piano roll, a playlist and a mixer

description.p: Spinus is a free, open-source digital audio workstation for Linux and Windows with an FL Studio-style workflow: build beats in the Channel Rack, write melodies in the Piano Roll, arrange patterns and audio on the Playlist and mix them in a mixer with as many inserts as you need.

ul.li: Step sequencer, piano roll with chord stamps and note tools, playlist with takes, and a clip launcher for jamming
Its own Sampler, Drum Machine, 3x Osc, Beat Slicer, EQ, Compressor, Limiter and Gate, and Surge XT, LSP and Dragonfly as free downloads
VST3, CLAP, LV2 and VST2 plugins, and Windows plugins through Wine without manual setup
Audio recording from one microphone or many inputs at once
Optional AI help: an assistant that only changes your project when you approve, a pattern generator, hum-to-notes, a song analyzer and an automixer
Export to WAV, FLAC, MP3, Opus and AAC, as a full mix or stems

description.p: Spinus works fully without AI; the AI features are off until you turn them on.

screenshot.caption: The Channel Rack and the Piano Roll

description.p: The third alpha: the experimental Track creator writes whole songs, from a description or from reference songs, with your installed instruments, grouped and colour-coded channels and parts you choose. The Analyzer runs on Windows too, OpenAI-compatible connections work with newer models, and fixes for plugin scanning and for plugins that load their sounds late.

The second alpha: report a problem from the Help menu with the logs attached, zoom and follow the playing in the editors, FL Studio's editing keys, shortcuts in every window, the system's plugins in the Flatpak, three more free plugins, and fixes.
The first alpha, an early release for testers.
